## F01 Loop and built-in tools

- F01.loop-shape — Loop shape [supported, verified] The agent works through a series of tool calls, deciding what to do next based on the result of each action. It uses tools to search code, edit files, and run the terminal, then reads each result before its next step. A stop hook is called when the agent loop ends and can optionally auto-submit a follow-up user message to keep iterating. | ev: E-cursor-01439, E-cursor-03987, E-cursor-00902
- F01.turn-limits — Turn and step limits [supported, unverified] There is no limit on the number of tool calls Agent can make during a task. Stop-hook auto follow-ups have a default limit of 5 per script, configurable via loop_limit; setting loop_limit to null removes the cap. The same limit applies to subagentStop follow-ups. | ev: E-cursor-01571, E-cursor-00903
- F01.tool-inventory — Native tool inventory [supported, unverified] Agent tools include file editing, codebase search, terminal execution, and more. First-party tools cover reading files, editing files, running terminal commands, searching the web, and more. Hook matchers filter by tool type, with values including Shell, Read, Write, Grep, Delete, Task, and MCP tools in the MCP:‹tool_name› format. | ev: E-cursor-00058, E-cursor-00071, E-cursor-00847
- F01.shell-tool — Shell execution tool [supported, unverified] Cursor runs shell commands directly in your terminal; Run Mode controls when commands run, when Cursor asks, and when terminal commands enter the sandbox. By default Cursor uses the first terminal profile available and requires your approval before executing any terminal command. The LocalAgentOptions cwd is the primary working directory for the default shell. | ev: E-cursor-01663, E-cursor-01577, E-cursor-00568, E-cursor-01372
- F01.file-edit-tools — File read, edit and write tools [supported, unverified] The built-in ToolCall union covers shell, edit, read, write, glob, grep, ls, semSearch, mcp, task, and others. A search tool can search for files by name, read directory structures, and find exact keywords or patterns within files. afterFileEdit fires after the Agent edits a file. | ev: E-cursor-03803, E-cursor-01572, E-cursor-00894
- F01.web-tools — Web search and fetch tools [supported, verified] A Web tool generates search queries and performs web searches. For the web fetch tool, without an allowlist entry each fetch prompts for approval, and domains added to allow are auto-approved. An Auto-Accept Web Search permission lets the agent run web searches without pausing for approval each time; it is off by default. | ev: E-cursor-01573, E-cursor-00333, E-cursor-00152

## F02 Context and memory

- F02.context-window-size — Context window size [partial, verified] Cloud Agents let you select the context window size; a larger window can increase token usage and costs. A subagent model string such as claude-opus-5[context=300k] sets the context window to 300k tokens. On request-based plans, Max Mode enables larger context windows. | limit: Automations use each model's maximum supported context window because they run as cloud agents. - F02.auto-compaction — Automatic compaction [supported, unverified] When the context window gets close to full, Cursor compresses older parts of the conversation into a summary to leave more room for new conversation. The preCompact hook is called before compaction and is observational: it cannot block or modify the compaction behavior. | ev: E-cursor-00061, E-cursor-00909
- F02.manual-compaction — Manual compaction [supported, verified] /summarize summarizes the conversation to reduce context and frees up space in the context window; /compress is an alias. A changelog entry says /summarize was renamed from /compress, and /compact and /compress remain as aliases that execute directly. | ev: E-cursor-00348, E-cursor-01892, E-cursor-01761
- F02.context-inclusion — Context inclusion controls [supported, unverified] Adding sensitive paths to .cursorignore keeps them out of the agent's context. beforeReadFile is called before Agent reads a file and can block sensitive files from being sent to the model. The dirs option adds workspace folders for multi-root setups, so rules, skills, and workspace context load from every path. | ev: E-cursor-00478, E-cursor-00895, E-cursor-01199
- F02.persistent-memory — Persistent memory [supported, unverified] Automation memories let the agent read and write persistent notes across runs for the same automation, stored as named entries (MEMORIES.md by default). Commenting @cursor remember [fact] on a PR makes Bugbot save a learned rule and apply it to future reviews. Conversation search lets Agent query past conversations. | ev: E-cursor-02045, E-cursor-01712, E-cursor-03979
- F02.memory-scope-loading — Memory scope and loading [supported, verified] Each Project maintains a set of files that sync across every cloud and local machine its agents use. ## F05 Sandbox and network isolation

- F05.os-sandbox — OS or container sandbox [supported, verified] In Auto-review mode, other shell commands run in the sandbox when possible. Command execution sandbox settings are configured with /sandbox or --sandbox ‹mode› (enabled or disabled) and persist across sessions. Cursor-hosted cloud runs use an isolated VM with the repo cloned in. Agents run on the local machine by default. | ev: E-cursor-00078, E-cursor-00301, E-cursor-01222, E-cursor-00586
- F05.fs-write-scope — Filesystem write scope [partial, verified] When sandboxed, writes are limited to the working directory, temp directories and paths allowed in sandbox.json; reads are not restricted to the workspace. Sandbox type workspace_readwrite (default) gives read/write access in the workspace. Enterprise teams can prevent agents from modifying the .cursor directory. | limit: Local agents run with local.sandboxOptions.enabled: false by default; the agent can read and write the working directory, execute shell commands, and reach the network without restriction. | ev: E-cursor-01356, E-cursor-03598, E-cursor-00582, E-cursor-01353
- F05.network-policy — Network policy [partial, verified] Network egress controls restrict outbound traffic to a default set plus an allowlist, or to the allowlist only; enterprise admins can lock the policy org-wide. In the sandbox, --network enables network access (default: false). Cloud Agent network settings apply to Cursor-hosted Cloud Agents. | limit: Network settings apply to Cursor-hosted Cloud Agents. Local agents run with local.sandboxOptions.enabled: false by default and can reach the network without restriction. | ev: E-cursor-00476, E-cursor-00329, E-cursor-00458, E-cursor-01353
- F05.subprocess-containment — Subprocess containment [supported, unverified] On macOS, Cursor uses Seatbelt through sandbox-exec; a generated sandbox profile limits file access, network access, and other process behavior for the full subprocess tree. When the sandbox is enabled, the SDK constrains every shell tool call and shell-spawned process. Cursor injects environment variables into every sandboxed child process. | ev: E-cursor-00099, E-cursor-01355, E-cursor-00104
- F05.sandbox-override — Sandbox override [supported, unverified] If a sandboxed command fails on a sandbox restriction, such as a permission error, the agent can rerun it outside the sandbox, and the classifier reviews that rerun. Some commands need full system access and bypass the sandbox; Cursor indicates when a command runs outside the sandbox and asks for approval. Sandbox type insecure_none disables the sandbox entirely. | ev: E-cursor-00088, E-cursor-00096, E-cursor-03598

## F06 Hooks and lifecycle events

- F06.event-catalog — Event catalog [supported, verified] Hooks observe, control or extend the agent loop at lifecycle events, in three categories based on what triggers them. Supported hooks on cloud agents include preToolUse, beforeShellExecution and afterFileEdit, plus beforeSubmitPrompt, subagentStart / subagentStop and preCompact. Worker hooks include sessionStart and sessionEnd when a session claims and releases the machine. | ev: E-cursor-00520, E-cursor-00800, E-cursor-01921, E-cursor-02489
- F06.handler-types — Handler types [partial, verified] Hooks support two execution types: command-based (default) and prompt-based (LLM-evaluated). Cloud agents run command-based hooks from .cursor/hooks.json in the repository. | limit: On self-hosted workers, only command-based hooks run; prompt-based hooks do not run. The SDK docs say hooks are file-based only, with no programmatic hook callback. | ev: E-cursor-00814, E-cursor-02577, E-cursor-03831, E-cursor-01920
- F06.input-contract — Input contract [supported, unverified] Command hooks receive JSON input via stdin. All hooks receive a base set of fields in addition to their hook-specific fields, including conversation_id (stable ID of the conversation across many turns). On a claim, sessionStart input also lists the run's repositories via repo_urls and repos. | ev: E-cursor-00815, E-cursor-00857, E-cursor-00858, E-cursor-02580
- F06.output-blocking — Output and blocking semantics [supported, verified] Exit code 0 means the hook succeeded and its JSON output is used; exit code 2 blocks the action, equivalent to returning permission: deny. For permission hooks, invalid JSON or a response that does not match the hook's schema blocks the action. The nested permissionDecision and updatedInput map to permission and updated_input. failClosed can be set for critical hooks. | ev: E-cursor-00816, E-cursor-00817, E-cursor-01077, E-cursor-00786
- F06.matchers — Matcher semantics [supported, unverified] A matcher is a regex string that filters when a hook runs; an empty string or * matches everything. For beforeShellExecution it runs against the shell command string; for preToolUse / postToolUse / postToolUseFailure it filters by tool type (values include Shell, Read, Write, Grep, Delete, Task, and MCP:‹tool_name›); for subagentStart it runs against the subagent type. | ev: E-cursor-00843, E-cursor-00846, E-cursor-00847, E-cursor-00845
- F06.config-locations — Configuration locations [supported, unverified] User hooks are configured in ~/.cursor/hooks.json and project hooks in ‹project›/.cursor/hooks.json. Cloud agents run command-based hooks from .cursor/hooks.json in the repository (on Enterprise plans also team and enterprise-managed hooks). Hook events carry an optional cursor.plugin.name when the hook came from a plugin. Cursor can also load hooks configured for Claude Code. | ev: E-cursor-00824, E-cursor-01920, E-cursor-00682, E-cursor-01071
- F06.trust-enable — Trust and enable controls [supported, verified] Project hooks load and run automatically when team members open the project in a trusted workspace, and the workspace must be trusted to run them. Claude Code hooks load when the Third-Party Imports setting is enabled (on by default). A Hooks tab in Customize and a Hooks output channel show configured and executed hooks and errors. | ev: E-cursor-03110, E-cursor-03111, E-cursor-01072, E-cursor-03123

## F07 Managed and enterprise controls

- F07.managed-settings — Managed settings delivery [partial, verified] The Cursor editor and agent can be deployed to workstations with policies enforced through MDM, and ~/.cursor/permissions.json can be distributed through MDM to set the per-user MCP auto-run allowlist from a managed file. Team hooks are configured in the web dashboard and synced to all team members automatically. | limit: Enterprise-managed hooks and dashboard distribution require an Enterprise plan. | ev: E-cursor-00536, E-cursor-00602, E-cursor-00830, E-cursor-01075
- F07.policy-lockdown — Policy lockdown [supported, unverified] Enterprise team admins can lock the network access setting with the Lock Network Access Policy option, and control which MCP servers members may use through an MCP allowlist in the team dashboard (Enterprise only). A team-defined global Auto-review configuration takes priority and Cursor ignores user-level and project-level files. MDM can enforce policies such as allowed team IDs and extensions. | ev: E-cursor-00472, E-cursor-00600, E-cursor-00086, E-cursor-00537
- F07.model-allowlist — Model allow and deny lists [supported, verified] Enterprise teams can control which AI models team members can use (contact sales to get access). Admins approve specific models for the organization; non-ZDR models require admin approval. On Enterprise, if a model is blocked for the team, Cursor Router routes to an allowed model, and a subagent's configured model is not used when an admin has blocked it. | ev: E-cursor-00589, E-cursor-00779, E-cursor-00508, E-cursor-01415

- F07.data-retention — Data retention and privacy [partial, verified] Enterprise customers can enroll in US-only data residency. - F07.admin-audit — Admin audit and reporting [supported, unverified] Admins are advised to periodically review audit logs and stream them to a SIEM. Skills package domain knowledge, workflows, and scripts in SKILL.md files. ## F09 Subagents and custom agents

- F09.definition-format — Definition format [supported, verified] Custom subagents are markdown files added to .cursor/agents/; plugin agents are markdown files in agents/. The model field in a subagent's YAML frontmatter can be set to a specific model ID; custom subagents default to inherit, which uses the parent agent's model. In the cloud API each custom subagent entry requires name, description and prompt, plus an optional model. | ev: E-cursor-03976, E-cursor-01457, E-cursor-03575, E-cursor-00390
- F09.tool-allowlist — Tool allow-list [partial, verified] The SDK tools option allowlists the built-in tools offered to the model, and disallowed_tools removes tools and keeps the rest. In a subagent definition, readonly: true (default false) runs the subagent with restricted write permissions (no file edits, no state-changing shell commands). Subagents can be configured with custom prompts, tool access, and models. | limit: SDK tools and disallowed_tools: both are local agents only for now, and neither persists on the agent; pass them again on resume. | ev: E-cursor-01184, E-cursor-01410, E-cursor-01468
- F09.per-agent-model — Per-agent model [supported, verified] A subagent's model field takes inherit (the default) or a specific model ID. Custom subagents default to inherit, using the parent agent's model, unless the model field in the YAML frontmatter sets one. Cloud Agent API customSubagents entries also take an optional model. | ev: E-cursor-01409, E-cursor-01457, E-cursor-00390
- F09.per-agent-effort — Per-agent effort [supported, verified] Appending square brackets to a model ID sets per-model options such as speed, reasoning effort and context window, written as id=value pairs. For example, claude-opus-5[effort=high] sets reasoning effort to high. | ev: E-cursor-01412, E-cursor-01413
- F09.nesting-rules — Nesting rules [partial, verified] Since Cursor 2.5, subagents can launch child subagents within a nesting limit, forming a tree of coordinated work. The main agent and its direct subagents can launch subagents. The Python SDK docs state the same rule. | limit: A subagent launched by another subagent can't launch further ones (E-cursor-01432). Side chats: 'Nesting is not supported. A side chat cannot spawn its own side chats.' (E-cursor-04224) | ev: E-cursor-01432, E-cursor-01182, E-cursor-04224
- F09.built-in-agents — Built-in agent types [supported, unverified] Cursor includes three built-in subagents (Explore, Bash, Browser) that handle context-heavy operations. Built-in subagents select their model automatically based on the subtask; the Explore subagent runs in its own context window with a faster model. Custom subagent names cannot collide with built-ins (explore, debug, shell, computerUse, etc.). | ev: E-cursor-01401, E-cursor-01457, E-cursor-00116, E-cursor-00391

## F10 Slash and custom commands

- F10.built-in-commands — Built-in commands [supported, verified] Built-in slash commands include `/model [filter]` (select a model; press Tab to edit), `/in-cloud` (the next task you submit runs as a cloud subagent on its own VM and branch), `/agent-review` (trigger a review on demand) and `/side` or `/btw` (open a side chat). | ev: E-cursor-00335, E-cursor-01426, E-cursor-01542, E-cursor-01589
- F10.custom-command-format — Custom command format [supported, unverified] Commands are reusable prompts invoked with `/` in Agent chat; they are markdown files that define a focused workflow or action. Custom commands are defined in a `.cursor/commands` directory. The plugin reference says commands support `.md`, `.mdc`, `.markdown` and `.txt` extensions and can include YAML frontmatter. | ev: E-cursor-00521, E-cursor-03513, E-cursor-03578
- F10.arguments — Arguments [supported, verified] Built-in commands take their argument after the command name: `/side` or `/btw` can be followed by your question in the chat input, and `/model [filter]` selects a model (press Tab to edit). | ev: E-cursor-01589, E-cursor-00335
- F10.discovery-paths — Discovery paths [supported, unverified] Commands are scoped to teams, projects, or users, and team admins can create organization-wide commands that appear for all developers. Custom commands are defined in a `.cursor/commands` directory; plugin commands are discovered in `commands/` as all `.md`, `.mdc`, `.markdown`, or `.txt` files. | ev: E-cursor-02961, E-cursor-03513, E-cursor-03565
- F10.command-skill-relation — Relation to skills [supported, unverified] Skills can also be manually invoked by typing `/` in Agent chat. Setting `disable-model-invocation: true` makes a skill behave like a traditional slash command, included only when you explicitly type `/skill-name`. Built-in `/migrate-to-skills` (Cursor 2.4+) converts eligible rules and commands to skills; slash commands become skills with `disable-model-invocation: true`. | ev: E-cursor-03937, E-cursor-03955, E-cursor-04320, E-cursor-03897

- F12.client-support — Client support [supported, verified] MCP lets you connect external tools and data sources to Cursor. The CLI detects and respects your `mcp.json`, enabling the same MCP servers and tools as the editor. Instructions and catalog from connected MCP servers count toward context. | ev: E-cursor-00599, E-cursor-00995, E-cursor-01885, E-cursor-00066

- F12.tool-filtering — Tool filtering and naming [supported, unverified] CLI permissions control which MCP tools the agent can run, using `server` (from `mcp.json`) and `tool` name with `*` wildcards. ## F13 Sessions, checkpoints, rewind

- F13.resume-continue — Resume and continue [supported, unverified] `--continue` continues the previous session (alias for `--resume=-1`); `--resume [thread id]` continues an existing thread and loads prior context. Conversation state, metadata and artifacts are saved to Cursor-managed storage so you can review and resume the run. Each subagent execution returns an agent ID to resume it with full context preserved. | ev: E-cursor-00312, E-cursor-01895, E-cursor-02313, E-cursor-03964
- F13.fork-branch — Fork or branch a session [supported, unverified] `/fork` forks the current chat into a new session. - F13.transcript-storage — Transcript storage [supported, unverified] Cursor stores agent chat history locally; conversation state, metadata and artifacts are also saved to Cursor-managed storage. ## F15 Background, scheduled and cloud-delegated work

- F15.background-tasks — Background tasks [supported, verified] Setting is_background: true (default false) runs a subagent in the background without blocking the parent. Background agents are coding agents that typically run for a very long time, moving a task from the local device to the cloud. A background subagent's result returns to the parent as a follow-up turn on the same run (local agents only). | ev: E-cursor-01411, E-cursor-04013, E-cursor-01183
- F15.scheduled-routines — Scheduled routines [supported, verified] Automations run cloud agents in the background on a schedule or in response to events. Timer subscriptions are a one-off reminder after a delay or a recurring cron schedule. The built-in `/loop` skill runs a prompt or skill on a recurring or variable interval; if you don't specify a fixed interval, the agent chooses when to wake. | ev: E-cursor-02012, E-cursor-02138, E-cursor-01594, E-cursor-04059
- F15.cloud-agents — Cloud agents [supported, unverified] The Cloud Agent API can create a Cloud Agent and immediately enqueue its initial run. Runs are listed as a Cloud machine, a Team Pool, or one of My Machines, and agents work in full development environments: they install dependencies, run tests, and verify their changes. Cloud Agents auto-run terminal commands so they can iterate on tests without stopping for approval on every step. | ev: E-cursor-00370, E-cursor-00451, E-cursor-00475
- F15.remote-sessions — Remote sessions [supported, unverified] You can take control of the agent's remote desktop to interact with the software it is building, and hand control back at any time. Agents keep working in the cloud whether or not your device stays connected. My Machines lets a specific user run Cloud Agent tool calls on a machine they already use: a laptop, devbox, or remote VM. | ev: E-cursor-02115, E-cursor-00453, E-cursor-02463
- F15.event-triggers — Event triggers [supported, verified] Automations run cloud agents in response to events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Linear, and more. Commenting `@cursor` on a GitHub PR or issue, or a Bitbucket PR, kicks off an agent. An agent can subscribe to an event source, end its turn, and wake on a matching event. The PR pushed / updated trigger runs an agent when new commits are pushed to an existing PR. | ev: E-cursor-02012, E-cursor-01909, E-cursor-02133, E-cursor-00122
- F15.delegation — Delegation to other agents [supported, unverified] Subagents are specialized AI assistants that Cursor's agent can delegate tasks to; each operates in its own context window and returns its result to the parent agent. `/in-cloud` hands a task to a cloud subagent, so long-running work runs on its own VM and branch. In a Project, a coordinator agent plans the work and delegates it to other agents. | ev: E-cursor-01395, E-cursor-01552, E-cursor-01570

## F19 Modes and autonomy levels

- F19.named-modes — Named modes [supported, verified] The CLI --mode flag takes plan or ask, with agent as the default. ## F22 Usage, cost, limits and observability

- F22.usage-visibility — Usage and cost visibility [supported, verified] The Spending dashboard shows request-level cost and pool details. The context ring next to the prompt input shows how full the window is; its breakdown tray shows total tokens used by category. `getUsage` fetches billed token usage and dollar cost for the agent, and an API endpoint retrieves token usage for an agent broken down per run. | ev: E-cursor-01508, E-cursor-00062, E-cursor-01253, E-cursor-01956
- F22.budget-caps — Budgets and caps [supported, unverified] You'll be asked to set a spend limit when you first start using Cloud Agents. Team limits are pooled usage plus admin-only controls. A group's settings page includes Spend Limit Overrides. When the Other Models allowance runs out on a Teams or Enterprise plan, own-key requests keep working if on-demand usage is enabled and stop until the next billing cycle if it is off. | ev: E-cursor-00369, E-cursor-00535, E-cursor-01530, E-cursor-01450
- F22.rate-limits — Rate-limit behaviour [supported, unverified] At the usage limit you'll see a notification in the editor and can enable on-demand usage (pay-as-you-go) or upgrade to a higher plan. Balance and Intelligence use your usage limits faster than Cost. One endpoint is rate limited to 300 requests per minute and 6000 per hour. Back off using exponential delay (the SDK reports `isRetryable: true` for transient cases). | ev: E-cursor-04414, E-cursor-02802, E-cursor-00416, E-cursor-03858
- F22.telemetry-otel — Telemetry and OpenTelemetry [partial, verified] OpenTelemetry Export streams usage metrics and logs to your observability stack over OTLP. Everything is on by default for a new destination except `conversation_content`, and individual families can be turned off in Team Settings. All metrics are monotonic delta sums. Starting a worker with `--management-addr` exposes `GET /metrics`, `/healthz` and `/readyz`. | limit: OpenTelemetry Export is listed as "(Enterprise only)". | ev: E-cursor-02857, E-cursor-00620, E-cursor-00664, E-cursor-02648

## F23 Request and response handling

- F23.prompt-assembly — Prompt assembly [partial, verified] SDK `systemPrompt` on `Agent.create()` replaces Cursor's built-in system prompt for the main agent loop. The model loses the coding-assistant identity, tool-use protocol and communication guidance; tool schemas, rules and skills still load and subagents keep their own prompts. Must be non-empty. Agent docs list instructions as the system prompt and rules. | limit: Only the SDK `systemPrompt` option is documented: local agents only (combining it with `cloud` throws `ConfigurationError`), not persisted (pass it again on `Agent.resume()`), and access is enabled per account. | ev: E-cursor-80004, E-cursor-80015, E-cursor-80005, E-cursor-80006, E-cursor-80014, E-cursor-80046, E-cursor-80047
- F23.prompt-caching — Prompt caching [partial, verified] The SDK reports prompt-cache use in token usage: `cacheReadTokens` (tokens served from the prompt cache) and `cacheWriteTokens` (tokens written to it), and `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_write_tokens` in the Python SDK. Model pages price cache reads and writes, for example Fable 5.1 cache reads at $0.25 per million tokens. | limit: Only usage counters and per-model cache prices are documented; no cache lifetime, invalidation rule or on/off/tune setting appears in the sweep hits. | ev: E-cursor-80048, E-cursor-80049, E-cursor-80050, E-cursor-80051
- F23.retry-backoff — Retry and back-off [partial, verified] CLI: dropped and stalled streams, including silent mid-stream stalls caught by HTTP/2 keepalive pings, retry automatically in all modes; transport and network-unreachable errors retry with backoff, show a 'Reconnecting' indicator and a hint if the network stays down. Subagent turns use the same policy. SDK: an option, default `true`, enables transport and stall auto-retry for local agent runs. | limit: Documented for the CLI and for SDK local agent runs; attempt limits and delay values are not stated, and rate-limit errors are described as shown with their real message, not as retried. | ev: E-cursor-80001, E-cursor-80002, E-cursor-80003, E-cursor-80052, E-cursor-80053, E-cursor-80054, E-cursor-80055
- F23.malformed-call-recovery — Malformed call recovery [undocumented, verified] swept for: malformed; invalid (tool|json|argument|parameter|input)|unknown tool|tool (call|use) (error|fail|invalid); schema validation|failed to parse|could not parse|unparseable; hits 10, reviewed 10; positive control `cursor`: 4578 hits
- F23.tool-output-limits — Tool output limits [partial, verified] SDK tool-call messages and the Cloud Agent API stream carry a `truncated` flag when `args` or `result` is too large (the API omits that field). CLI long shell output truncates from the top, and shell mode truncates large outputs automatically. Browser logs are written to files the agent greps and reads selectively. | limit: Per surface: SDK and Cloud Agent API stream payloads (no size given), CLI shell output, and browser tool logs. No size limit or setting for tool output entering the model context is given in these quotes. | ev: E-cursor-80007, E-cursor-80009, E-cursor-80039, E-cursor-80056, E-cursor-80057
- F23.output-redaction — Output redaction [partial, verified] Cloud Agent Runtime Secrets are redacted from tool call results, chat transcript and commits. Shared transcripts get best-effort redaction of known secret patterns. OpenTelemetry export scrubs message text, shell commands and MCP tool I/O: credential shapes, PEM blocks, SSNs and emails become `[REDACTED: ...]`; values under keys like `password` or `token` are redacted. | limit: Per surface: Cloud Agent Runtime Secrets; shared transcripts ("best-effort", "not guaranteed"); Enterprise OpenTelemetry export of Cursor's Grok Bot records ("best effort"). Redaction of local agent tool output is not described. | ev: E-cursor-80023, E-cursor-80026, E-cursor-80028, E-cursor-80030, E-cursor-80043, E-cursor-80058, E-cursor-80059
